name: FUTURES MATTER COMMUNITY INTEREST COMPANY
description: The purpose or objects of the Company are to carry out activities which relate to and will benefit the community in general. The primary focus of the company will be the positive long-term outcomes for Looked-after or vulnerable children. Long standing research and statistical data clearly indicates that there are poor long term outcomes for this group in our society. The outcomes we aim to achieve:  1. Improving the engagement of the child in education, 2. To address gaps in education 3. Continuity in education  We aim to recruit and train a team of 15 - 20 'Educational mentors' with a social care / teaching background to work with the child, school, social services and other partner agencies. This team will provide the key service that will form the bridge between agencies, placements, and the child. They will be allocated on a long-term basis, their focus will be around looking at the child's educational experience and to advocate for consistency, a high level of provision, additional services and if necessary, the provision of additional teaching / tuition. A key aspect of the mentor's work will be around their focus on the needs of the child, this could mean pushing for more in-depth assessments of the child's needs, particularly if there are underlying issues such as dyslexia.  The second component of the service will be around providing additional tuition based upon the children / young people's individual needs. It is the aim of the service to be able to both identify and offer some provision in this area, particularly in view of the pressures on school and education establishments around the provision of such additional funding. It is also a factor that by being able to provide some limited, additional tuition the positive impact on the child may be demonstrated and so prove the case for the need of additional support to the child on a longer-term basis.

name: BORO DOUGHNUT C.I.C.
description:
1) Primarily residents of Middlesbrough and the surrounding area of Tees Valley.  Our aim is for the town to adopt the Doughnut Economics model that is regenerative and distributive by design, so that they can meet the needs of all people within the means of the living planet.  This means we help disadvantaged people who do not have basic necessities such as food, education, health, social networks, housing and energy as we highlight the actual state of the town using evidence-based quantitative and qualitative data.  The residents' voice will be reflected in the 'City Portrait'.  We create opportunities for community engagement with policy makers, academics and other non-profit organisations to support progress in the town's Green Strategy.  Using the 'CIty Portrait', we can work on the gap between the town's target and the reality.  By collaboration, we promote the existing good initiatives and tackle the root cause of problems identified, and aim for the town as a whole to align to our Doughnut vision.  We also tackle each of the categories such as waste management to voice residents' concerns about health & safety and unfair provisions in more deprived areas of Middlesbrough.  2) Those who are socially isolated, those who need space and the opportunity to enhance wellbeing, School pupils in deprived areas around Berwick Hills, Special Needs groups such as Autistic children and community as a whole (intergenerational/racial/social groups mingling for the common goal of the Doughnut.) We have been invited to manage the Council owned Edible Forest Garden in Berwick Hills.  This has been abandoned for many years, but we aim to create a permaculture educational space.  It will benefit those who want to engage in mindfulness, learn about permaculture, forest schools and use the space as a meeting place.  3) Resident communities in Middlesbrough and the Tees Valley and beyond. The Doughnut Economics teaches us to think before we act using the Four Lenses - not only looking at the wellbeing of all people and the environment in our local community, but also globally. (i.e, circular economy) We are providing workshops and events to promote this vision and introduce practical ways to learn from solutions that are there already, and encourage them to join in the community action.  4) Community artists and creatives We believe that the idea of Doughnut Economics would not spread effectively without the power of the Arts.  We will be giving artists, musicians, poets, dancers, social media creators etc. opportunities to express the vision of Doughnut Economics through arts.

Investment in resources and a programme of accessible information-giving that helps create genuine understanding and offer people real opportunities to make a difference for future generations.Enhancing permaculture space (Edible Forest Garden) listening to community voice.  Events to promote Doughnut Economics/circular economy solutions.  Workshops for community engagements and other agencies (policy makers, town offices, academics, other non-profits).  Forest and Eco School promotions and support.  Website, social media, posters etc to promote Doughnut Economics.  Yorkshire network project - collaborations with other regions striving for circular economy and Doughnut Economics.  Waste management solution E.g. Paints for bins - community involvements in circular economy messages on public bins)  Setting up circular economy system such as repair cafe, timeshare, sharecycle.  Coffee morning etc sustainable cookery, edible garden, permaculture, mindfulness sessions etc.

description: At the JPC Community Hub C.I.C, our mission is to support adults with special and complex needs to live more independently and engage meaningfully with the world around them1 particularly within our local community, which experiences significant social deprivation.
